item.title: Operativo nocturno con helicóptero en Quito y despliegue policial deja detenidos, armas y droga incautada
item.author: Marjorie Ortiz
item.description:
Operativo nocturno con helicóptero en Quito y despliegue policial deja detenidos, armas y droga incautada
2026-09-12
Por Marjorie Ortiz
https://www.primicias.ec/seguridad/helicoptero-policia-quito-detenidos-armas-droga-clausura-bares-132451/
Operativo nocturno con helicóptero en Quito y despliegue policial deja detenidos, armas y droga incautada
El sobrevuelo de helicópteros en la zona del centro y norte de Quito llamó la atención de ciudadanos la noche del 11 de septiembre de 2026, mientras la Policía atribuye operativo al Plan de Protección en la capital.
Imagen que muestra algunos de los productos decomisados durante un operativo de seguridad realizado por la Policía Nacional el viernes 11 de septiembre del 2026
- Foto
API
Autor:
Redacción Primicias
Actualizada:
Compartir:
Un operativo policial que incluyó el sobrevuelo de helicópteros y el despliegue de más de un centenar de agentes de seguridad sorprendió a los quiteños la noche del viernes 11 de septiembre del 2026, mientras fuentes policiales lo atribuyeron al Plan de Protección de Quito que logró la detención de tres personas, además de armas y droga incautada.
En diferentes sectores de Quito como La Pradera, La Mariscal o la avenida Eloy Alfaro o las inmediaciones del parque La Carolina, los ciudadanos reportaron desde pasadas las 20:00 la presencia de helicópteros que iluminaban desde la altura las calles y barrios de la capital.
“Ya van varios minutos que escucho que sobrevuelan helicópteros y muchas sirenas por el sector de La Pradera, alguien sabe qué ha pasado”, comentó una usuaria en las redes sociales, mientras que otro ciudadano agregó: “Qué onda el helicóptero que anda volando por el centro norte de Quito”.
Algunos moradores subieron a sus redes sociales imágenes y videos en los que se observaba el sobrevuelo de las aeronaves sobre las edificaciones de la ciudad y mostraron satisfacción por las acciones de seguridad. “Eso deben hacer siempre por todos los rincones de Quito y Ecuador”.
“Más y más operativos”, “Excelente”, señalaron otros usuarios, aunque también hubo quienes cuestionaron que los operativos se concentren en las zonas del centro y norte. “Alguna vez harán eso en el sur y no solo en lugares para la foto”, criticaron.
Mientras tanto, el jefe de operaciones del Distrito Eugenio Espejo, Byron Flores, confirmó que estas acciones se realizan con frecuencia y actualmente corresponden al Plan de Protección de Quito, anunciado por el gobierno para reducir los delitos en la capital.
“El operativo fue interinstitucional, estuvo encabezado por Policía Nacional en el distrito Eugenio Espejo, no fue a nivel de Quito, que lo conforman el casco comercial, se desarrolló en Cochapamba, Nayón, Iñaquito y La Mariscal”.
Byron Flores, jefe de operaciones del Distrito Eugenio Espejo.
En el operativo participaron las Fuerzas Armadas, Aduanas, la Agencia Metropolitana de Tránsito (AMT), comisarías, y se contó también con el apoyo logístico de un helicóptero.
“Lo que se pretende con el uso del helicóptero es patrullar desde el aire, porque muchas veces lo que no se avanza a ver en tierra, el helicóptero nos ayuda un montón. Hicimos varios sobrevuelos en la parte del hipercentro de Quito para verificar algunas novedades”, indicó.
Una agente policial agregó que “el helicóptero llamó la atención bastante porque comenzó a sobrevolar un poco más bajo, con luces más a tierra. Yo estaba en el operativo y escuchaba a la gente que decía ‘de ley algo pasa’, ‘algo está sucediendo’, pero el helicóptero es patrullaje aéreo, muchas veces hacemos vigilancia con drones”, indicó la policía.
También se hizo una intervención policial en el sector de La Pradera, una zona residencial que desde hace varios años se ha convertido en zona rosa, con la presencia de bares, discotecas, restaurantes. Los agentes hicieron controles a personas, registros en los locales, etc.
Estos operativos se realizan de manera permanente, señaló el mayor Flores, sin embargo, resaltó que las

Algunos moradores subieron a sus redes sociales imágenes y videos en los que se observaba el sobrevuelo de las aeronaves sobre las edificaciones de la ciudad y mostraron satisfacción por las acciones de seguridad. “Eso deben hacer siempre por todos los rincones de Quito y Ecuador”.
“Más y más operativos”, “Excelente”, señalaron otros usuarios, aunque también hubo quienes cuestionaron que los operativos se concentren en las zonas del centro y norte. “Alguna vez harán eso en el sur y no solo en lugares para la foto”, criticaron.
Mientras tanto, el jefe de operaciones del Distrito Eugenio Espejo, Byron Flores, confirmó que estas acciones se realizan con frecuencia y actualmente corresponden al Plan de Protección de Quito, anunciado por el gobierno para reducir los delitos en la capital.
“El operativo fue interinstitucional, estuvo encabezado por Policía Nacional en el distrito Eugenio Espejo, no fue a nivel de Quito, que lo conforman el casco comercial, se desarrolló en Cochapamba, Nayón, Iñaquito y La Mariscal”.
Byron Flores, jefe de operaciones del Distrito Eugenio Espejo.
En el operativo participaron las Fuerzas Armadas, Aduanas, la Agencia Metropolitana de Tránsito (AMT), comisarías, y se contó también con el apoyo logístico de un helicóptero.
“Lo que se pretende con el uso del helicóptero es patrullar desde el aire, porque muchas veces lo que no se avanza a ver en tierra, el helicóptero nos ayuda un montón. Hicimos varios sobrevuelos en la parte del hipercentro de Quito para verificar algunas novedades”, indicó.
Una agente policial agregó que “el helicóptero llamó la atención bastante porque comenzó a sobrevolar un poco más bajo, con luces más a tierra. Yo estaba en el operativo y escuchaba a la gente que decía ‘de ley algo pasa’, ‘algo está sucediendo’, pero el helicóptero es patrullaje aéreo, muchas veces hacemos vigilancia con drones”, indicó la policía.
También se hizo una intervención policial en el sector de La Pradera, una zona residencial que desde hace varios años se ha convertido en zona rosa, con la presencia de bares, discotecas, restaurantes. Los agentes hicieron controles a personas, registros en los locales, etc.
Estos operativos se realizan de manera permanente, señaló el mayor Flores, sin embargo, resaltó que las

item.title: Cisma en el correísmo: 37 asambleístas van al Consejo de Disciplina de Revolución Ciudadana por su votación en la Ley de Adopciones
item.author: Roberto Rueda
item.description:
Cisma en el correísmo: 37 asambleístas van al Consejo de Disciplina de Revolución Ciudadana por su votación en la Ley de Adopciones
2026-09-12
Por Roberto Rueda
https://www.primicias.ec/politica/asambleistas-correismo-consejo-disciplina-revolucion-ciudadana-votacion-ley-adopciones-132097/
Cisma en el correísmo: 37 asambleístas van al Consejo de Disciplina de Revolución Ciudadana por su votación en la Ley de Adopciones
La coordinadora de la bancada correísta, Patricia Núñez, los acusa de incumplir una decisión adoptada por órganos directivos. Entre los denunciados están figuras del correísmo, como Viviana Veloz y Ricardo Patiño.
Asambleístas de la bancada de Revolución Ciudadana previo al inicio del debate y aprobación de la Ley de Adopciones el 28 de julio de 2026.
- Foto
Asamblea Nacional.
Autor:
Redacción Primicias
Actualizada:
Compartir:
Un mes y medio después de aprobarse en la Asamblea Nacional la Ley de Adopciones, las repercusiones para los legisladores de la Revolución Ciudadana (RC) que apoyaron la norma del oficialismo podrían empezar.
La coordinadora de la bancada correísta, Patricia Núñez, denunció ante el Consejo de Disciplina y Ética de la organización política a 37 de sus integrantes, entre los que se encuentran Ricardo Patiño, Viviana Veloz y Xavier Lasso.
Los acusa de no haberse acogido a la disciplina del movimiento y desacatar una decisión adoptada en torno a esta normativa que fue aprobada el 28 de julio pasado con el voto de 118 asambleístas, entre ellos, correístas.
¿Cómo se dieron los hechos?
En la bancada de RC existe un equipo de seguimiento jurídico que se encarga de analizar desde el primer momento cada uno de los proyectos de ley que ingresan a la Asamblea Nacional.
Su trabajo consiste en presentar un informe final a la bancada con los puntos a favor, en contra, los que se pueden mejorar y las líneas rojas de la propuesta. Incluye una recomendación de cómo debería votar el correísmo.
En este caso, como en otros, la sugerencia fue que RC no debería apoyar el documento elaborado por la Comisión de Transparencia, que está liderada por Diana Jácome de Acción Democrática Nacional (ADN).
En una sesión virtual, en la que participaron unos 38 legisladores correístas, se tomó la decisión de votar en abstención, lo que habría sido ratificado por la propia presidenta del movimiento, Gabriela Rivadeneira, a través de una llamada telefónica, según pudo conocer PRIMICIAS.
Sin embargo, minutos antes de que se produzca la votación el 28 de julio, algunos asambleístas se acercaron a Nuñez para informarle su voluntad de votar a favor del texto de la Ley de Adopciones impulsado por ADN.
En esta línea se habrían ubicado asambleístas como Pamela Aguirre, Paola Cabezas, Blasco Luna, Luis Molina, Jahiren Noriega, Mónica Palacios, Héctor Rodríguez, Franklin Samaniego, quienes ya fueron notificados.
Eso puso en entredicho el liderazgo de Núñez al interior de la bancada y de la propia Gabriela Rivadeneira como dirigente máxima de la Revolución Ciudadana.
Las posibles sanciones
El Régimen Orgánico del Movimiento Revolución Ciudadana contempla la posibilidad de que sus militantes y adherentes puedan cometer faltas leves y faltas graves.
La faltas leves se sancionan a través de una amonestación escrita y suspensión de los derechos del adherente por un tiempo máximo de seis meses.
En tanto que, si la falta es considerada grave, las sanciones internas en RC pueden ser:
- Suspensión por el tiempo de seis meses a dos años según el alcance de la falta.
- Expulsión definitiva del Movimiento sin perjuicio de sanciones civiles, disciplinarias o penales que dieran lugar.
- Perder el derecho a ser candidata o candidato por el movimiento en el próximo proceso electoral de elección de dignidades y ocupar cargos dentro del movimiento.
"Es un tema interno"
La denuncia presentada por Patricia Núñez ante el Consejo de Disciplina y Ética de la Revolución Ciudadana solo confirma los rumores del malestar al interio
[Transcripcion recortada]

item.title: El testigo del caso Villavicencio contra José Serrano acepta ser extraditado a Estados Unidos
item.author: Redacción Primicias
item.description:
El testigo del caso Villavicencio contra José Serrano acepta ser extraditado a Estados Unidos
2026-09-12
Por Redacción Primicias
https://www.primicias.ec/politica/rphr-testigo-villavicencio-extradicion-estados-unidos-132170/
El testigo del caso Villavicencio contra José Serrano acepta ser extraditado a Estados Unidos
El exagente de inteligencia RPHR consintió su extradición a Estados Unidos durante la audiencia instalada en la Corte Nacional de Justicia. Se trata de un testigo clave en la causa del magnicidio de Fernando Villavicencio, donde incriminó al exministro José Serrano y a Daniel Salcedo.
Audiencia extradición RPHR el 9 de septiembre de 2026.
- Foto
Captura de la audiencia
Autor:
Actualizada:
Compartir:
Durante la audiencia de extradición pasiva ante la Corte Nacional de Justicia, el exteniente RPHR aceptó, de viva voz, ser entregado a Estados Unidos. El requerido formalizó su consentimiento tras ser consultado por el presidente del organismo, Marco Rodríguez, y confirmar su defensa legal.
RPHR, exagente de inteligencia policial, es testigo clave en el expediente del magnicidio de Fernando Villavicencio. En sus declaraciones, señaló al exministro José Serrano Salgado por ordenar vigilancias y rastreos a la víctima previos al crimen de agosto de 2023.
La jornada en la Corte Nacional continuará esta tarde con la audiencia de extradición de Daniel Salcedo Bonilla. Salcedo, sentenciado en Ecuador por tramas de corrupción, es solicitado por las autoridades estadounidenses dentro de indagaciones por delincuencia transnacional.
Ambos sujetos están relacionados en el expediente judicial del caso Villavicencio. Salcedo habría reclutado a RPHR en prisión para ejecutar los seguimientos a Villavicencio y facilitó los contactos con Serrano, actuando como el nexo entre la cúpula política y los grupos criminales.
De agente de inteligencia a testigo clave
RPHR ingresó a la Policía Nacional en marzo de 2013 y dos años después se integró a la Unidad de Inteligencia Antidelincuencial (UIAD).
En 2019 fue condenado a 34 años y ocho meses de prisión por un delito en Cuenca, pero recobró la libertad en septiembre de 2022 tras un hábeas corpus. Ya fuera de prisión, habría sido contactado por Daniel Salcedo para ejecutar seguimientos de inteligencia a Fernando Villavicencio.
Sus señalamientos lo convirtieron en un testigo clave del magnicidio de agosto de 2023, al incriminar al exministro José Serrano por supuestamente encomendarle la vigilancia de la víctima. Hoy Serrano está preso en la Cárcel del Encuentro, junto a Salcedo y RPHR.
Durante su audiencia en la Corte Nacional de Justicia, RPHR aceptó ser extraditado a Estados Unidos. Todavía no se conocen los detalles de su caso en ese país.
Su consentimiento estuvo precedido por una alerta de seguridad. El investigado denunció que su primo fue asesinado en Guayaquil 15 días atrás tras conocerse el pedido norteamericano, solicitando la reserva de su imagen e identidad.
Compartir:

item.title: Los carros de Japón están en el top 3 de los más vendidos en Ecuador; estos son los modelos más demandados
item.author: Evelyn Tapia
item.description:
Los carros de Japón están en el top 3 de los más vendidos en Ecuador; estos son los modelos más demandados
2026-09-12
Por Evelyn Tapia
https://www.primicias.ec/economia/ecuador-acuerdo-comercial-japon-carros-japoneses-modelos-132010/
Los carros de Japón están en el top 3 de los más vendidos en Ecuador; estos son los modelos más demandados
El Presidente Daniel Noboa manifestó el interés de Ecuador de buscar un acuerdo comercial con Japón. Si se logra el acuerdo, uno los beneficios podría ser la reducción de aranceles para los carros japoneses.
Imagen referencial de un local de venta de carros japoneses en el norte de Quito, archivo.
- Foto
PRIMICIAS.
Autor:
Redacción Primicias
Actualizada:
Compartir:
Ecuador mira a Japón para un eventual acuerdo comercial. El pasado 4 de septiembre de 2026, el mismo presidente Daniel Noboa reiteró el interés:
"En los últimos 10 años (Japón) se ha vuelto menos competitivo versus Corea y China, y ha visto que sus exportaciones han caído y ya no pueden seguir así. Entonces tienen que abrirse un poco al mundo" lo que implica ampliar importaciones y exportaciones, comentó Noboa.

item.title: SpaceX signs another AI computing deal, with $100 billion in ARR 'on track,' CFO says
item.author: Pras Subramanian
item.description:
SpaceX signs another AI computing deal, with $100 billion in ARR 'on track,' CFO says
2026-09-12
Por Pras Subramanian
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/spacex-signs-another-ai-computing-deal-with-100-billion-in-arr-on-track-cfo-says-152933886.html
SpaceX (SPCX) just inked another big AI compute deal, one that will take the space and rocket company closer to its $100 billion annual recurring revenue (ARR) target this year, a big metric for investors.
At the Goldman Sachs Communacopia & Technology Conference in San Francisco, CFO Bret Johnsen said a new AI compute deal has been reached in which SpaceX leases out compute bandwidth for third-party clients.
"We're on track, or we believe we're on track to hit $100 billion ARR," Johnsen said about SpaceX's overall ARR target, as AI compute deals helped fuel the growth, before revealing the news. "What I would tell you, an update to that is that just earlier this month we closed another hosting deal, and that translates into about $1.11 billion a month starting December 1st of this year, which is another roughly $13 billion of ARR."
Add this to deals already in place, and SpaceX's compute deals are creating a nice revenue stream. Earlier this year, SpaceX announced a compute deal with Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) for $1.25 billion per month ($15 billion ARR) and another deal with Alphabet's (GOOG, GOOGL) Google for $920 million per month ($11.04 billion ARR).
In a note to clients, William Blair analyst Louie DiPalma confirmed that the new deal differs from the $6.7 billion, six-month deal ($13.4 billion ARR) that was announced on SpaceX's August earnings call. "We suspect the $6.7 billion/6-month deal that was announced on the earnings call is with the U.S. Department of Defense," he said.
DiPalma explained why SpaceX is winning with its AI compute business.
"SpaceX has benefited from its ability to deploy capacity much faster than peers to take advantage of the unprecedented demand environment for compute capacity," DiPalma said. "In addition, SpaceX has benefited from its close relationship with Nvidia, which provides SpaceXAI with priority allocation to GPUs."
The four deals noted here — without mentioning any other deals SpaceX has in place — amount to around $45.7 billion in ARR for December. Add the rocket business (approximately $4 billion in ARR based on Q2 earnings) and the Starlink division ($17.2 billion), and it seems possible that $100 billion could be reached as growth continues, with Johnsen saying he has "even more conviction" in hitting that goal.
One wrinkle in its AI compute game plan is that SpaceX is now considering slowing the physical build-outs of its terrestrial data centers to help address operational and reliability concerns, per The Information.

item.title: Anthropic Says US Adversaries Aimed Claude at Weapons Research
item.author: Olivia Solon; Jordan Robertson; Ryan Gallagher
item.description:
Anthropic Says US Adversaries Aimed Claude at Weapons Research
2026-09-12
Por Olivia Solon; Jordan Robertson; Ryan Gallagher
https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/anthropic-says-us-adversaries-aimed-120427318.html
(Bloomberg) -- Anthropic PBC says its artificial intelligence model Claude has been misused in attempts to develop a wide range of potential military applications, including kamikaze drone swarms, missile navigation systems and biological weapons.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Users from countries including Iran, Russia, China and Yemen are among those flagged for misusing the AI company's frontier models in the past year, according to a report by Anthropic's threat intelligence team on Thursday. None of the cases involved Anthropic's most advanced models, Fable and Mythos.
"As models become increasingly capable, their risks will increase, unless AI developers and society's defenders act to make them safer," Anthropic said in the report.
US AI companies have been racing to develop and deploy more capable AI systems, in part to stay ahead of rivals like China, while trying to maintain safeguards. Anthropic is seeking to prevent its technology from being used for harmful purposes, including the development of biological and conventional weapons.
That position brought it into direct conflict with the Pentagon, which suspended work with Anthropic after it refused to allow Claude to be used for mass surveillance or autonomous weapons systems.
The report says users have attempted to deploy Claude to help America's enemies. In many cases they tried to evade Claude's safeguards or conceal their locations.
Users in Russia, which Anthropic determined were not linked to the state, tried to use Claude to build software for an autonomous, first-person-view, kamikaze drone swarm trained on Ukrainian combat footage.
The report also details five case studies of people using Claude in ways that could support the development of biological weapons, including state-sponsored virologists looking to create an enhanced version of a debilitating mosquito-borne virus called chikungunya. The effort was identified through a request for Claude to help write a grant application to fund research at a military institute in an unnamed country where Anthropic doesn't provide service.
Anthropic noted that all of the biological case studies in the report were "ambiguous" and involved research that could have benign scientific intent.
Actors based in Houthi-controlled northern Yemen, however, used Claude to build software for several types of missiles.
"We do not have evidence the actors succeeded in fielding an operational device," Anthropic said.
State-linked actors in countries including China and Iran tried to use Claude to build and facilitate surveillance. One China-linked operation used Claude to "track, profile and recruit Uyghurs" in the Syrian Army. An Iranian unit used Claude to build surveillance software disguised as a tool to keep track of prayer times. China's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
In another case, it discovered that a consultant likely working for a state intelligence agency in Mali had used Claude to build a system designed to monitor roughly 25 million mobile phones in the West African country. The system could generate "intelligence dossiers" on any specified phone number, without a court order. Anthropic said that it banned the consultant's account, but that the Claude-powered surveillance platform had been deployed locally and was out of the company's full control. The Malian government did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Anthropic's report also highlighted how hackers — ranging from suspected state-sponsored intelligence in Russia and China to hacktivists and cybercriminals — are using the company's AI to speed up and amplify their efforts to steal sensitive data. The report does not reveal any novel or dangerous new vulnerabilities in criti
[Transcripcion recortada]

One China-linked operation used Claude to "track, profile and recruit Uyghurs" in the Syrian Army. An Iranian unit used Claude to build surveillance software disguised as a tool to keep track of prayer times. China's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
In another case, it discovered that a consultant likely working for a state intelligence agency in Mali had used Claude to build a system designed to monitor roughly 25 million mobile phones in the West African country. The system could generate "intelligence dossiers" on any specified phone number, without a court order. Anthropic said that it banned the consultant's account, but that the Claude-powered surveillance platform had been deployed locally and was out of the company's full control. The Malian government did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Anthropic's report also highlighted how hackers — ranging from suspected state-sponsored intelligence in Russia and China to hacktivists and cybercriminals — are using the company's AI to speed up and amplify their efforts to steal sensitive data. item.title: Fed’s Rate Decision May Have Come Down to Phone Plan Changes
item.author: Jeffrey Sparshott; Matthew Boesler
item.description:
Fed’s Rate Decision May Have Come Down to Phone Plan Changes
2026-09-12
Por Jeffrey Sparshott; Matthew Boesler
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/fed-rate-decision-may-come-154304847.html
(Bloomberg) -- A record jump in the price of cellular phone services helped tip a key measure of US inflation above forecasts, likely sealing the deal for a Federal Reserve interest-rate increase next week.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The consumer price index excluding food and energy climbed 0.3% in August from a month earlier, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data out Friday. The median estimate in a Bloomberg survey called for a 0.2% increase. The 5.9% surge in wireless telephone services prices alone added about a 10th of a percentage point to the core reading.
That gauge largely reflects prepaid and monthly plans offered by cellular carriers.
Economists at Bank of America Corp., Barclays Plc and Pantheon Macroeconomics flagged recent plan changes by major carriers like AT&T Inc. and T-Mobile US Inc. as likely culprits. The BLS declined to elaborate on how the changes at those carriers may have impacted the number.
AT&T said earlier this year that it would implement price increases on certain plans in August. T-Mobile also recently retired some of its legacy plans, resulting in price increases for consumers.
Even so, many Fed-watchers still saw a case for raising interest rates, even if underlying inflation was lifted last month partly by one-time factors.
"While it is true that the wireless index added 10bps to the core CPI today, and that the core ex-wireless would have been 0.20%, I don't think the Fed will have the luxury of slicing and dicing the data at the meeting next week," Omair Sharif, president of Inflation Insights LLC, said in a note.
--With assistance from Kelcee Griffis.
Most Read from Bloomberg Businessweek
2026 Bloomberg L.P.

item.title: Trump’s ‘Golden Age’ Confronts Economic Angst That Threatens GOP
item.author: Josh Wingrove
item.description:
Trump’s ‘Golden Age’ Confronts Economic Angst That Threatens GOP
2026-09-12
Por Josh Wingrove
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/articles/trump-golden-age-confronts-economic-173000047.html
(Bloomberg) -- The Republican faithful, gathered in arena hallways and hotel ballrooms during this week's midterm convention, projected confidence they had a good story to tell on the economy.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Some pointed to the steady unemployment rate and stock market growth as evidence of a new "Golden Age" driven by a resilient economy and American consumer, while others argued immigration and manufacturing policies were yielding a better life for US citizens.
Still, a latent anxiety hung over Dallas. The reality — that polls suggest voters are in fact quite anxious about the state of the economy, and preparing to punish Republicans in November's midterm elections — has become hard for even President Donald Trump to ignore.
Ultimately, the way voters feel about an economy that is a mess of contradictions - growing and stable but expensive and inequitable — seems likely to dictate the results of the vote, and, consequently, how much longer Trump can single-handedly reshape the federal government.
Fuel prices are surging up, despite the end of the summer travel season. Data out Friday showed little progress on inflation last month, which investors and economists say will likely lead the Federal Reserve to hike rates next week over Trump's public objections.
Consumer sentiment slid below estimates in September, with consumers expecting prices will continue to rise. Just 35% of Republicans in the University of Michigan survey believe the government is doing a good job with the economy, the lowest reading since Trump returned to the White House last year.
Peppered throughout the president's celebration of his second-term accomplishments was a growing, albeit, tacit admission of needing to do more to reassure voters: by acknowledging some victories could take time to manifest, and by dangling the prospect of a $5,000 "Trump dividend." Pressed as he departed the convention on why such a payment was necessary if the economy was thriving, Trump told reporters he intended it as a "reward" for those who had suffered during President Joe Biden's presidency. But he allowed that conditions hadn't immediately improved upon his taking office.
"They had to put up with the four years, and that carried on at least half an additional year," Trump said.
Vice President JD Vance's keynote Thursday nodded to outrage over housing costs, imploring Republican voters to stick with the party even if they don't agree on everything. US 30-year mortgage rates climbed to a one-year high earlier this week; prior to the Iran war, costs for home borrowing had fallen to their lowest level since 2022.
Trump was an inescapable presence over the two nights, speaking twice from the stage, sitting for a Fox News interview, chatting with traveling reporters and hosting high-dollar fundraisers.
He insisted to all that would listen that things were good.
Growth, Trump argued in a Fox News interview, could not only pay for his $1.2 trillion dividend giveaway but help address a national debt that in recent weeks has surpassed $40 trillion, roiling the bond market. Inflation is elevated, but not nearly as high as seen during the Biden administration. The extension of his signature tax cut law — and new provisions giving seniors an additional break and removing federal taxes on some tips — meant tax returns were higher. Prescription drug prices have in some cases ticked down.
"We've had record employment in this country," said Ray Washburne, the Sunoco LP chairman who co-chaired the committee staging the convention in Dallas. "We're having boom times in a market like this, and I think that shows the rest of the country what can be done."
But framing the economy as humming along is a risky gamble.

item.title: Rising Bond Yields Are Driving US Stocks Toward Correction Territory: Markets Pulse
item.author: Kerry Benn
item.description:
Rising Bond Yields Are Driving US Stocks Toward Correction Territory: Markets Pulse
2026-09-12
Por Kerry Benn
https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/rising-bond-yields-driving-us-093100638.html
(Bloomberg) -- The escalating bond selloff is driving US Treasury yields toward levels that threaten to deal a significant blow to the stock market, according to the latest Markets Pulse survey.
Most Read from Bloomberg
Around 30% of the 122 people who responded to the poll by Bloomberg said 10-year yields hitting 5% to 5.25% would be enough to set off a 10% drop in stocks from their peak, a decline that would meet the definition of a correction. 22% pegged the range slightly higher, at 5.25% to 5.5%.
The benchmark 10-year yield climbed on Thursday to over 4.96%, a fresh three-year high, as the conflict President Donald Trump unleashed in the Middle East pushed oil well over $100 a barrel, raising the specter of a worsening inflation shock and a response from the Federal Reserve.
"One would think that we are on the cusp of a long-anticipated correction in the equity market as actual data and central bank policy provide a potent reality check for risk-loving investors," said Joseph Brusuelas, RSM chief economist.
The Treasury rate, a key benchmark for the cost of money in the wider economy and the valuation of equities, has already sparked concern in the Trump administration with November's midterm elections nearing. Survey participants cited accelerating price pressures and fiscal concerns as the top threats to Treasuries over the next six months.
The key yield has climbed a full percentage point since Trump starting bombing Iran at the end of February and is hovering just below the roughly 5% peak last hit in late 2023, after the Fed wrapped up the interest-rate hikes aimed at taming the post-pandemic inflation surge.
The latest rise is coming instead as traders brace for the Fed to start raising rates again as soon as next week, with new Chairman Kevin Warsh under pressure to show he's prepared to act on his pledge to rein in inflation that's held over the bank's target since 2021.
If Warsh does lead the Fed in a hike, more than 80% of survey participants think that will be part of a one- or two-time mid-cycle adjustment rather than the beginning of a larger series of increases.
A steady stream of solid earnings reports have so far overshadowed the impact of higher rates, with the S&P 500 Index not far below last month's record highs despite a 2% slide over the past four days.

item.title: Global Bond Selloff Sends 10-Year Treasury Yields to Cusp of 5%
item.author: Cameron Fozi; Greg Ritchie
item.description:
Global Bond Selloff Sends 10-Year Treasury Yields to Cusp of 5%
2026-09-12
Por Cameron Fozi; Greg Ritchie
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/global-bond-selloff-sends-10-001324539.html
(Bloomberg) -- Bond bears are pushing benchmark Treasury yields toward the closely-watched 5% level ahead of US inflation data that stands to determine expectations for a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike next week.
Most Read from Bloomberg
The yield on 10-year notes climbed 18 basis points this week to trade just below the psychologically-important level, which may attract dip buyers but also risks triggering further selling that could spill over into global markets. At 4.96% on Friday, the yield has reached the most-elevated level since 2023 — and is approaching its highest since 2007.
The surge in yields comes as traders wrestle with rising oil prices and inflation that's run above the Federal Reserve's target for half a decade. A reading of the US consumer price index Friday stands to be one of the most pivotal in years as traders price in a roughly 70% chance of a rate increase at the Sept. 16 Fed meeting.
"Hitting 5% on the 10-year Treasury yield looks more like an inevitability here than a forecast," said Padhraic Garvey, head of research for the Americas at ING Groep NV. "These are worrying times for bond markets."
Yields on the two-year, which are more sensitive to Fed rate moves, rose to as high as 4.59% this week. Thirty-year yields hit their highest since 2007, luring standout demand at an auction of the securities.
The moves have spilled over into bond markets worldwide, with Australian benchmark yields hitting their highest since 2011 on Friday and Japanese equivalents trading close to the key psychological level of 3%. A gauge of global yields is at its highest since 2007.
"A lower US CPI and a Fed hike are really the only circuit breakers I see at this point, otherwise I don't think anyone is comfortable being long rates," said Michael Tang, a rates strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia in Sydney. "It's just massive hawkish sentiment taking over."
That leaves traders on edge going into Friday's main economic event — especially as Fed officials have underscored their focus on inflation in recent weeks. To Molly Brooks, a US rates strategist at TD Securities, a hotter-than-expected print stands to boost market expectations for a hike in September and additional tightening.

2026-09-11
Por Aditi Bharade
https://businessinsider.com/trump-stop-canada-bombardier-sold-us-2026-9
President Donald Trump doesn't want one particular Canadian aircraft crossing over into the US.
In a Truth Social post on Monday, Trump wrote: "No more selling Bombardier in the United States! Their products aren't good enough."
Trump said that if the company wants business from the US, it needs to build its jets in the US. Bombardier, an aircraft manufacturer based in Montreal, makes business and private luxury jets.
US federal agencies such as the US Air Force and the Federal Aviation Administration were previously reported to have Bombardier aircraft in their fleets. Representatives for the White House did not respond to a query from Business Insider on whether any federal agencies are canceling orders with Bombardier after Trump's announcement.
Bombardier wrote in a statement on its website on Monday, without any reference to Trump's post, that it's a "strong contributor" to the American aerospace industry, creating "tens of thousands of jobs across the United States."
The statement said that Bombardier's American workers are based across the US, with sites in Kansas, Texas, Arizona, Florida, Connecticut, Illinois, Delaware, California, Washington, D.C., and New Jersey. It has "overall direct employment presence in more than 20 states," Bombardier said.
The company said it also uses American-made aircraft components in its manufacturing, like engines, wings, and avionics. Its supply chain includes 2,800 American companies across 47 states, it added.
"Bombardier values its great partnership with American companies and its U.S. employees," the company said in the statement. "Our plan is to continue to invest in our people, our customers, and the communities in which we operate across the country."
Trump's post comes as trade tensions between the two neighbors flare. Canada's latest round of tariffs went into effect on Tuesday, imposing 50% duties on hundreds of US goods, including cheese, honey, and aluminum foil. These levies are a retaliatory response to the 50% tariffs the US imposed on Canadian products such as dairy, alcohol, and electronics.

item.title: US consumer sentiment deteriorates in September, inflation expectations rise
item.author: Reuters
item.description:
US consumer sentiment deteriorates in September, inflation expectations rise
2026-09-11
Por Reuters
https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/articles/us-consumer-sentiment-deteriorates-september-142448698.html
WASHINGTON, Sept 11 (Reuters) - U.S. consumer sentiment deteriorated in early September as rising gasoline prices and trade tensions stoked fears of higher inflation over the next 12 months, a survey showed on Friday.
The University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers said its Consumer Sentiment Index dropped to 47.8 this month from 51.7 in August. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the index at 51,0. Sentiment sagged among consumers identifying as Democrats and Republicans, but was little changed among Independents.
"With a resurgence in fuel prices and trade tensions, consumers anticipate greater pressures on their pocketbooks to come," said Joanne Hsu, the director of the Surveys of Consumers.
The survey's measure of consumer expectations for inflation over the next year jumped to 4.6% from 4.0% last month. Twelve-month inflation expectations were at 3.4% in February before the U.S.-led war with Iran started. Consumers' expectations for inflation over the next five years edged up 3.4% from 3.3% in August. They are higher than their 2024 range of 2.8% to 3.2%.
(Reporting By Lucia Mutikani; Editing by Chizu Nomiyama )
